It also shows up over here in my 3D window as the red internal shape. ## Applications of Internal Shapes Pretty cool, right? You’re probably thinking, "Oh my gosh, that is really cool!" But what can I do with it? What can't you do? There are so many things you can do with this now. You can use this for creating embossed graphics, patch graphics, or anything like that. I can select these internal lines, right-click, and choose **Clone as Pattern with Sewing**. It’s cloned! What you might have also noticed is this: I can select this, right-click, copy, and then paste it right into here. After that, I can right-click and **Convert to Whole**. You might be wondering, “Phoebe, that didn’t do anything.” But it did! I just have a shape inside. Look at that! Now, I’m just going to quickly sew this. To save my computer a little bit, I’ll right-click and superimpose over it. I’ve created a really cool detail! Let’s set it to see if you can see this. This is going to be a really cool design with a lot of possibilities. ## Color and Textures So now that you have set that up, let’s see what happens. I have a pattern here, and on the left, I can see the pattern centimeters. I can just drag and drop that into the picture. You can see how easy this is with this little method! Let me go ahead and start this again. That's really cool! I can also, because now they are pattern pieces, make them any color I want. I could say, “This is shiny,” or “I could make it a velvet.” You can really do a lot of things now with this! Also, if you wanted to, you could right-click and **Cut**, right? Then you could cut this all out and delete these parts. Just make sure you cut and sew this to that. Delete these so that they act as a true part of the design. You can do so many different things; it’s really up to you. I could make this plastic, right? I could add pressure to it. There are so many things you can do to make your graphics look more realistic and cooler. It's all out there! ## Production Considerations Here’s something you might not think about: you could also use this when it comes to production. Let me open up my other file. Right before we move on to other techniques, I just want to show you what happens if you have a graphic with a white background or other backgrounds and how that will work.
